| Ceiling | Margin | Why this margin |
|---|---:|---|
| working set against memory | 25% | Past the limit, memory cannot hold the whole working set, so some reads go to disk. A request's time then includes waiting for those reads, and the model has no term for that wait, so the service time per request is no longer the number this model was built on. Nothing in a chain of multiplications says what it becomes (ch08), and the margin is the working set's own daily swing. |
| utilisation, counting coordination | 30% | This ceiling keeps the queueing margin, the same margin as the ceiling labelled utilisation at the busy hour. It applies the margin to the capacity the fleet can deliver, counting coordination, rather than to the capacity its hosts would have alone. Where the two ceilings disagree, this one is about the system you own (ch07). |
| disk fill at horizon | 25% | A fleet whose disks are full cannot take a dead host's records. A filesystem needs free space to keep allocating well, and the margin carries this as an assumption rather than a measurement. The margin is the same node the sizing used, so the two cannot drift apart (ch11). Over the limit means out of space; inside the margin means the re-replication reserve has been spent on data. |
| utilisation with one host down | 30% | One host down at the busy hour: its share of the requests lands on the survivors, and the question is whether they are still inside the queueing margin. N+1 is this ceiling with the margin at zero. The margin here is the queueing margin, because a fleet that has lost a host is still a queue (ch11). |
| utilisation at the busy hour | 30% | Not a capacity limit: a fleet that is busy most of the time, but short of fully busy, has not run out of anything; it has a queue in front of it. The margin is large because crossing it is paid for in waiting time by every request, not in a failure that pages the people on call (ch06). |
| fraction of the fleet doing nothing useful | 50% | At the margin, half the fleet's work is lost: one host in two does no useful work. The loss is to contention and to coordination between hosts. Nothing fails and nothing pages anyone; the fleet costs twice what its work is worth. A budget is the only thing this ceiling protects (ch07). |
